We have an older house with a combination NuTone Vent-A-Lite Bathroom Fan Model 8672. After sorta fixing it several times, we bought this, along with a Kitchen Basics 101 5901A000 Fan Blower Wheel Assembly Replacement for Broan NuTone and the two worked perfectly. Two quick pieces of advise- READ THE INSTRUCTIONS that come with the blower wheel (there's a flat side on the motor shaft that needs to be aligned), and second, make sure the blower wheel is slightly farther down on the shaft than the end. I set it in flush the first time and it rubbed against the housing. I moved it down a few millimeters and it cleared it just fine and now it works great. These two items avoided having to deal with the whole mess of resizing the opening/ducting and taking a chance on a new fan for much more money. Works like new now.
Super easy to install. Saved me the aggravation of replacing current fan light.

My significant other and I tend to greatly appreciate classic items that are still extremely functional. It would have been easier to buy a modern exhaust fan for the kitchen (and quite possibly more efficient) but we both enjoyed the visual appeal of our home’s original (1952) kitchen exhaust fan. The old motor was beat. It finally quit. This motor was a perfect replacement. She is a professional chef that cooks daily at home. An exhaust fan is essential for us. We were very happy to find a motor that fit perfectly in the constraints of something that was designed lifetimes ago. The only modification that needed to be made was the plug end. It comes with a 90* plug that just wouldn’t work for our application. I was able to adapt the original plug end into the new motor. We are very happy with this purchase.
Very easy to install, great price and fast shipping

I purchased motor and squirrel cage fan hoping to quiet bathroom exhaust fan. It’s much quieter than before. It’s not as quiet as a modern exhaust fan but easier to install and much cheaper. Good move!

Pulled an ancient (installed 1969), dead, possibly fossilized bathroom exhaust NuTone fan apart. Rust, crud and corruption. Looked for a replacement on Amazon; incredibly there it was.
A perfect fit EXCEPT the shaft on this motor is a tad longer than the original. Rather than grind the shaft down, I installed some washers to lift the mounting bracket up enough (~1 scosche which was maybe 2 washers ea. bolt) so the shaft would clear the back of the exhaust sheet metal. Ta-da.

Sure as can be, it fits and works perfectly and matches OE specs! My fan/light unit is a Nutone MH-8661N (or maybe MH-866IN). I assume the MH prefix is for Mobile Home? In any case, if you are looking for one, this is it!

My bathroom fan was making a lot of noise when turning it on, but then would sound normal after a second or so. I removed the fan motor assembly from the housing and inspected the fan to be loose from the motor. Everything appeared to be tight, so I assumed the motor was the issue. When the new motor arrived, I re-installed the fan to the motor shaft and still had the noise when plugging in. Upon inspecting closer, the motor shaft was slipping inside the plastic fan. What I really needed was a new plastic fan, but I ended up wedging a shim between the fan and motor drive shaft to get a better connection. Posting so that hopefully someone else doesn’t make the same mistake.

Had a 70's style Nutone bathroom fan that would start very slowly. Thought just replacing the fan motor would be the easiest route. Fan fit the frame well, but this thing is loud, like thee times as loud as the original. Can hear it in the next room over, and wasn't the case with the old motor. I cleaned the fan and mounts with simple green before reinstall. Obviously a cheap Chinese knock off motor. Been thinking of trying some 3in1 oil or SAE30 weight oil on the old motor shaft cause it was so much quieter, oh and the original was made in Cincinnati so go figure it was much better quality. I may try replacing the rubber grommets but that would be another $40 for both top and bottom mounts. The original mounts were in good shape no cracks or splits other than being 50 years old. Motor is better than nothing but far cry from the original motor.

I love the flexibility a Keurig machine gives you to use your own ground coffee. I grind my whole beans and use 3-4 aftermarket mesh filters to enjoy it using the Keurig. What I didn't enjoy was the fine silt that I would find in the bottom of my cup. I found these unbleached(healthier) k-cups and -- problem solved! They are the best practical solution for my needs. Easy to use, take up very little storage space and allow me to enjoy my coffee w/o any grit or silt.

Have you ever woken up in the middle of your REM cycle and you NEED coffee to touch your soul to wake you up? So, you make your coffee as you normally do, a little bit more excited today becuase you got these new Disposable Natural Brown Unbleached Paper Coffee Filters from Amazon. You add your oat milk and maple syrup because even though you like your coffee sweet, you try your best to be sustainable Your eyes are still droopy and full of sleep as you waft the aroma of your freshly brewed coffee - the day will be good. Your robe is cozy, your slippers are comfy, you get ready for your first sip... BAM COFFEE GROUNDS ALL IN YOUR MOUTH. ITS LITERALLY MORE GROUNDS THAN WATER AT THIS POINT. UPDATE:
I am no longer able to use these filters. My old Keurig brewed its last, and I bought a new one. This new machine recommends the Keurig brand insert for using your own beans, and the paper filter does not fit in this (nor do my old inserts). Of note, before I bought the new machine, I purchased a different type of insert for my old machine. While the filter fit in this, it was essentially useless, as the mess it left was not worth it. Overall disappointed that my quick clean-up trick is gone.

I found these liners after someone brought them to my work. I originally thought "Hmm...seems like a waste of money". I was wrong. I drink 2 cups of coffee at work every day. These filters are fabulous little time savers. After brewing a cup of coffee, the liner pops out of my reusable K cup and GREATLY reduces the clean up time. In fact, a quick rinse of the top (yes, I probably over fill it) and I'm good to go. If I skip the rinse, its no big deal, the cup is that clean.

I suspect the people who are having trouble with more grounds than coffee are not using the liner properly. It's meant to be a liner for a reusable K cup and not for use on its own. I too made this mistake the first time I used the liner alone, and what a mess! While not a necessity, when used properly, its a great time saver.
